To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed novel feature engineering techniques for clinical text classification that utilize the taxonomic structure of the UML and that we have demonstrated the utility of our methods on a large scale clinical text classification task.

we developed novel feature engineering techniques for clinical text classification that leverage the taxonomic structure of the UMLSto improve feature ranking, that we developed a semantic kernel for classification that projects clinical text to a feature space to improve classification, and that these methods improve upon the results achieved by the top machine-learning based systems in the I2B2 obesity challenge.

we developed novel information-theoretical methods that leverage the taxonomical information encoded in the Unified Language System to improve feature selection, and developed a novel semantic similarity measure to improve text representation.

developing methods for clinical text classification that leverage the biomedical knowledge encoded in the UMLS.
the development of methods for clinical text classification using machine learning.

the following questions: (i) how to use UMLS to improve clinical text classification; (ii) what is the impact of using a domain knowledge-based feature ranking method on the performance of a text classification system; and (iii) what is the effect of context-dependent semantic similarity measures on the classification of clinical text.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods presented here improve the performance of the top machine-learning based clinical document classification system in the I2B2 challenge.
the methods developed in this study can improve machine-learning based classification of clinical text.

our work is the first to leverage the structure of the biomedical domain knowledge in the UMLS for clinical text classification, and the results show that this approach can improve the state-of-the-art in clinical text classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we used the UMLS to guide our feature engineering for clinical NLP.

the methods we developed leverage the structure of the Unified medical language system (UMLS) and the document class labels to improve feature ranking and semantic kernel construction for clinical text classification.

we have developed novel information-theoretical techniques that utilize the domain knowledge encoded in UMLS to improve feature ranking and semantic similarity measure for clinical text classification, and we have evaluated these methods on a real clinical text classification task, the 2008 I2B2 obesity challenge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
biomedical domain knowledge encoded as a semantic network can be utilized in a variety of ways to improve machine-learning systems for clinical text classification.
domain knowledge encoded in a biomedical terminology can be used to improve the performance of clinical text classification systems.
the UMLS can be leveraged for clinical text classification, and that the methods we developed are effective in improving classification performance.
